title: Formal export schema with validation, seq semantics, and versioned migrations
description:
The .json.gz export format is defined implicitly — whatever export_game.py emits and whatever consumers parse. No shared schema, no validation, no documented semantics for seq numbers or snapshot timing. This makes schema evolution risky: changing a field name or structure requires manually auditing every consumer and hoping nothing breaks.

Work items:

1. **Write a formal schema definition** for the v2 export format. Single source of truth (JSON Schema or Pydantic models) covering all top-level fields, snapshot structure, action types, llmEvent types, llmTrace structure, and gameOver. Document seq number semantics: the two independent namespaces (server seq vs per-player LLM seq), that multiple events can share a server seq, what a snapshot represents (game state at decision presentation time), and ordering guarantees.

2. **Validate on both ends.** The exporter (export_game.py) asserts its output conforms to the schema. Consumers assert their input conforms. Ideally with codegen: generate TypeScript types from the schema for website consumers so the schema definition is the single source of truth.

3. **Delete migrate_old_exports.py.** All games are already v2; the v1→v2 migration script is dead code.

4. **Build a migration framework** for future version bumps (v2→v3, etc.). Each version transition is a module with up() and down() transforms. CI roundtrip test: down(up(game)) == game for every exported game. Designed for incremental adoption: land the v3 schema first, migrate games across multiple PRs, delete migration code once complete. At most two versions coexist at any time.

See doc/export-schema.md for detailed seq semantics, consumer inventory, and design notes.
